title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, take buses and auto-rickshaws, and give instructions politely or casually.
intro:
Punjabi towns are navigated by landmarks — the chowk, the gurdwara, the big tree — more than by street names, so be ready to hear 'go straight from the clock tower and turn left after the bank'. This unit gives you places, transport words and the **imperative**, the verb form for instructions.

Remember that ਸਿੱਧਾ (*síddā*, straight) has a high tone and ਰਾਹੀਂ (*rā́īṃ*, via) too.

grammar.title: The imperative: ਜਾ, ਜਾਓ, ਜਾਇਓ
grammar.body:
Punjabi has several imperative forms, matched to the 'you' you are using:

**ਤੂੰ** (intimate): bare stem — ਜਾ! ਆ! ਬੈਠ! ਕਰ!
**ਤੁਸੀਂ** (polite): stem + **-ਓ** — ਜਾਓ, ਆਓ, ਬੈਠੋ, ਕਰੋ. Irregular: ਦੇ → ਦਿਓ 'give', ਲੈ → ਲਓ 'take', ਪੀ → ਪੀਓ.
**Softer / later**: stem + **-ਇਓ** — ਜਾਇਓ, ਕਰਿਓ, ਦੱਸਿਓ 'do tell (me later)'. Very common and friendly.
**Very polite**: the infinitive, often with ਜੀ — ਬੈਠਣਾ ਜੀ, ਦੱਸਣਾ ਜੀ.

Negative imperatives use **ਨਾ** (not ਨਹੀਂ): ਨਾ ਜਾਓ 'don't go', ਫ਼ਿਕਰ ਨਾ ਕਰੋ 'don't worry'.

Adding ਜੀ always softens: ਆਓ ਜੀ, ਬੈਠੋ ਜੀ.

examples.en: Give me a call when you arrive.
Could you please tell me the way?

grammar.title: Going to, from, via and up to
grammar.body:
With verbs of motion, the destination often needs **no postposition**: ਮੈਂ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ਜਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਹਾਂ 'I'm going to the market'. With people, use ਕੋਲ: ਡਾਕਟਰ ਕੋਲ ਜਾਣਾ 'to go to the doctor'. ਨੂੰ is sometimes used for 'to' a place, especially in the oblique: ਘਰ ਨੂੰ 'homewards'.

**ਤੋਂ** 'from' · **ਤੱਕ** 'up to, until' · **ਵੱਲ** 'towards' · **ਰਾਹੀਂ** 'via, through' · **'ਤੇ** 'on' (ਬੱਸ 'ਤੇ ਜਾਣਾ 'to go by bus'). Adverbs of place add -ਓਂ for 'from': ਇੱਥੇ → ਇੱਥੋਂ 'from here', ਉੱਥੇ → ਉੱਥੋਂ 'from there'.

dialogue.title: Taking an auto
dialogue.setting: Tom flags down an auto-rickshaw outside his hotel in Amritsar.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Brother, will you go to the Golden Temple?

lines.speaker: Tom

lines.roman: báut ziādā hai! sau ṭhīk hai?
lines.en: That's too much! Is a hundred OK?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: OK, a hundred and twenty-five. Get in.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ਹੌਲੀ ਚਲਾਇਓ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਜਲਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ।
lines.roman: haulī chalāio, mainūṃ koī jaldī nahī̀ṃ.
lines.en: Drive slowly please, I'm in no hurry.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ਆਹ ਚੌਕ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਗੱਡੀਆਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾਂਦੀਆਂ। ਇੱਥੋਂ ਪੈਦਲ ਜਾਓ।
lines.roman: ā́ chauk toṃ agge gaḍḍīāṃ nahī̀ṃ jāndīāṃ. itthoṃ paidal jāo.
lines.en: Vehicles don't go beyond this chowk. Walk from here.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ਹਾਂ, ਸਿੱਧੇ ਜਾਓ ਤੇ ਫਿਰ ਖੱਬੇ ਮੁੜੋ। ਪੰਜ ਮਿੰਟ।
lines.roman: hāṃ, sídde jāo te phir khabbe muṛo. panj minṭ.
lines.en: Yes, go straight and then turn left. Five minutes.

culture: Agree on the fare before getting into an auto-rickshaw. Drivers and shopkeepers are addressed as ਭਾਜੀ, ਵੀਰ ਜੀ or ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ (for a turbaned Sikh man). When asking the way, ask more than one person: people would rather give confident directions than admit they don't know! The walled old city of Amritsar around the Golden Temple is pedestrianised.

tip.title: Commands: ਜਾਓ, ਮੁੜੋ, ਦੱਸੋ
tip.body:
- To ਤੁਸੀਂ (anyone you don't know well) add **-ਓ** to the stem: ਜਾਓ 'go', ਮੁੜੋ 'turn', ਦੱਸੋ 'tell'.
- To a friend or child (ਤੂੰ) use the bare stem: ਜਾ, ਮੁੜ, ਦੱਸ.
- Add **ਜੀ** to soften it: ਦੱਸੋ ਜੀ 'please tell me'.
tip.pattern: ਸਿੱਧੇ ਜਾਓ  ·  ਸੱਜੇ ਮੁੜੋ  ·  ਦੱਸੋ ਜੀ

lessons.title: Near, far and how to get there

tip.title: From, up to, towards, via
tip.body:
- These words come **after** the place: ਚੌਕ **ਤੱਕ** 'up to the crossroads', ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ **ਵੱਲ** 'towards the market'.
- **ਤੋਂ** from · **ਤੱਕ** up to · **ਵੱਲ** towards · **ਰਾਹੀਂ** via.
- 'From here' is one word: ਇੱਥੇ → **ਇੱਥੋਂ**, ਉੱਥੇ → **ਉੱਥੋਂ**.
- Going *to* a place usually needs no word at all: ਮੈਂ ਬਾਜ਼ਾਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ.

lessons.title: Buses, trains and autos

tip.title: By bus, with a friend
tip.body:
- 'By bus / by train' = **'ਤੇ** 'on': ਬੱਸ 'ਤੇ, ਗੱਡੀ 'ਤੇ, ਆਟੋ 'ਤੇ.
- 'With someone' = **ਨਾਲ਼** after the person: ਦੋਸਤ ਨਾਲ਼, ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ਼.
- ਬੱਸ and ਗੱਡੀ are feminine, so 'it goes' is **ਜਾਂਦੀ** ਹੈ; ਆਟੋ is masculine: **ਜਾਂਦਾ** ਹੈ.

tip.title: Talking to a driver
tip.body:
- Ask **ਚੱਲੋਗੇ?** 'will you go?' and **ਕਿੰਨੇ ਪੈਸੇ ਲਓਗੇ?** 'how much will you take?'. Agree the ਕਿਰਾਇਆ 'fare' before you get in.
- Then just give polite commands: **ਰੋਕੋ** 'stop', **ਰੁਕੋ** 'wait', **ਚੱਲੋ** 'go on'.
- 'Don't' with a command is **ਨਾ**, never ਨਹੀਂ: **ਨਾ** ਰੁਕੋ.

sentences.en: Brother, will you go to the station?
What's the fare to the market?
Not a hundred: take eighty rupees.
Don't stop now, keep going straight.
Please stop just past the crossroads.
Wait two minutes, please.
Come on, let's go to the market.
What time does the train arrive?
When will we get there?

tip.title: I have to: ਉਤਰਨਾ ਹੈ
tip.body:
- Infinitive (-ਣਾ / -ਨਾ) + **ਹੈ** = 'I have to / I'm to': ਮੈਂ ਇੱਥੇ **ਉਤਰਨਾ ਹੈ** 'I have to get off here'.
- Ask the same way: ਮੈਂ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਉਤਰਨਾ ਹੈ? 'Where do I get off?'
- Get **on** = ਚੜ੍ਹਨਾ, get **off** = ਉਤਰਨਾ; with a vehicle use **'ਤੇ**: ਬੱਸ 'ਤੇ ਚੜ੍ਹਨਾ.

sentences.en: I have to get off at the station.
